values: Materials and settings｜all fictional de-identified paper-and-pencil exercises
A fictional organization has 120 item handover records and needs to check the record chain for one lost item; use only R numbers and do not write real names, location tracking, or account numbers.
A1: the engagement is limited to checking whether the handover ledger is complete; you may view the six pre-given fictional records and may not infer anyone's responsibility.

A3: the R1, R3, and R5 fields are complete; R2 is missing the time, R4 has an inconsistent item number, and R6 has a duplicated receipt number. The other 114 records were not observed.

A5: three of the six records have documented suspicions, a sample of 3/6=50%; this is not the error rate for all 120 records, and theft or a responsible person cannot be inferred.

description.text: Private detectives and investigators search data, interview, check timelines, and deliver traceable reports within the lawful engagement scope. See the United States O*NET 33-9021 occupational tasks and 2025 wages, the BLS 2025–2035 employment projection, the Chinese wage evidence gap, privacy risks, and the fictional entry exercises.

subject.name: Private detectives and investigators
subject.summary: Within a clearly defined engagement and the applicable legal boundaries, private detectives and investigators review materials they are permitted to use, interview relevant people, and check timelines, and they write verifiable facts and unverified claims into the report separately. The position carries no police powers; handling personal information, on-site observation, and data sharing all require first checking the legal basis and the scope of authorization.
